title: SRE weekly ops sync prep - 2026-03-04 (Alex Martin)
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync + reliability review. Keep it light; we’ll deep-dive only on >sev2 or burning error budget.

Agenda (20-30m):
1) Quick SLO health snapshot (5m)
2) Paging trends + oncall load (5m)
3) Top incidents (10m)
4) Action items & owners (5m)

SLO snapshot (last 7d) - quick bullets (source: SLO dashboard / PagerDuty analytics):
- Hosted API (text generation): availability SLO 99.95% (window 30d). Current 30d = 99.96% ok. 7d error budget burn = 1.8%.
- Latency SLO (API p99 <= 220ms). 7d p99 = 255ms (regression starting 2026-03-01). Error budget burn (latency) = ~5.6% last 7d.
- Dedicated endpoints: availability SLO 99.9%. 7d = 99.85% (small breach on 2026-03-01 due to GPU OOM cascade). Error budget burn = 4.2%.
- Embeddings service: SLOs all green (p95/p99 within target).
Notes: latency regression correlated with multiple small incidents (OOMs + model variant fallback) — see below.

Paging trends / oncall load:
- Avg pages/day last 14d: 9 -> up from baseline 7 (~+28%). Nighttime pages (00:00-06:00 UTC) increased 40% driven by dedicated capacity region eu-west-1.
- Top page reasons: model OOMs (36%), network flaps to dedicated hosts (22%), job scheduler failures for batch jobs (18%), false-positive alerts from shard-health check (10%).
- Oncall fatigue note: Jordan reported three overlapping pages Mon-Wed night; consider cooldown or runbook improvements.

Top incidents (last 7d) - for discussion:
1) incident-dedicated-gpu-oom-2026-03-01 (sev2)
   - Timeline: 2026-03-01 02:14 UTC high OOM rate on dedicated pool eu-west-1, noisy neighbor + new quantized-model variant rollout. Auto-failover triggered; some customer requests hit fallback models with higher latency.
   - Impact: 15% of dedicated traffic experienced elevated p99s (up to 1.2s). One customer reported SLA degradation and opened ticket JIRA-SRE-457.
   - Root cause (initial): memory regression in quantization kernels after recent runtime change (kernel selector bumped in 2026-02-28 deploy).
   - Mitigation: rolled back kernel selector change at 02:47 UTC, rebalanced pods, increased per-pod memory limit as temporary mitigation.
   - Next steps: engineering patch to kernel memory accounting (PR linked), add preflight mem-pressure test in CI for quantized variants.

2) incident-network-flap-dedicated-hosts-2026-03-03 (sev3)
   - Brief: transient network issue in eu-west-1 AZ B impacted scheduler heartbeats. Auto-evacuation worked but burst of scheduling churn caused latency blips.
   - Mitigation: improved backoff in scheduler and added cascade dampening (deployed canary 2026-03-04).

3) false-alerts-shard-health-checks-2026-03-02 (low)
   - Several false positives due to a threshold change in monitoring template. Noise contributed to page fatigue.
   - Action: revert threshold tweak + fix alert docs so oncall knows to ignore noise-based pages.

Open questions / things to validate before meeting:
- Can infra/release-eng confirm which canaries included kernel selector change (timeline)? (Jordan)
- Is the quantized-model CI mem-pressure test feasible to run nightly without blowing CI budget? (Samira)
- Should we lower alert sensitivity for shard-health checks during peak noise windows or instead improve dedup logic? (Ops)

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Alex: prepare 1-slide visual of p99 latency trend (hosted/dedicated) for the meeting. ETA: 2026-03-04 10:00 UTC.
- Jordan: chase release-eng for full deploy timeline & list of impacted canaries. Add to JIRA-SRE-457. ETA: 2026-03-04 EOD.
- Samira: feasibility + rough plan for nightly mem-pressure test for quantized variants. Draft plan in GH issue. ETA: 2026-03-06.
- Ethan: implement alert doc updates + revert shard-health threshold in monitoring. ETA: 2026-03-04 morning.
- Eng (release/serving-runtime): finish kernel memory-accounting patch + run soak on staging. Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912. ETA: 2026-03-09.

Runbook / playbook gaps noticed:
- No clear runbook for quantized-model memory regressions. Need a short checklist: how to detect, how to rollback, safe knobs to reduce memory. (owner: Samira)
- Lack of documented fallback SLAs for cache-warm vs cold fallbacks (affects p99 signoffs). (owner: Alex)

Prep notes for meeting facilitator (Alex):
- Start with high level SLO slide, call out the latency regression + error budget burn quickly.
- Ask release eng to own timeline discussion — avoid deep kernel-level debugging in ops sync; we want visible mitigations + timeline.
- Reserve 5 mins for oncall burnout / paging noise discussion — propose short-term: reduce noisy alerts, long-term: dedupe + improve runbook.

Misc notes / scratch ideas:
- Could add an "OOM early-warning" metric: mem-pressure trends per pool + recent deploy fingerprint to correlate.
- Consider weekly scheduled maintenance window for heavy quantized variant testing to avoid surprise regressions in prod.

Raw links / references:
- SLO dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/slo/dashboard
- Incident JIRA: JIRA-SRE-457 (customer SLA ticket)
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912
- PagerDuty incident summary: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-2026-03-01-oom

TODO (post-meeting):
- Consolidate action items into JIRA epic and assign owners (Alex)
- Draft a short postmortem note if kernel patch required (make decision within 72h if sev2 repeats).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep meeting under 30m. If deep dive needed, spin up a follow-up with runtime + release eng.
- Bring up possibility of customer communication for impacted Dedicated customers (CS/AM to own).
summary: Prep notes for SRE weekly ops sync on 2026-03-04: SLOs, paging trends, top incidents (OOM, network flap), action items and runbook gaps.
